text:
alex.cruz: Anyone seeing a customer in us-east-1 with inference streams failing after TLS handshake? Private VPC, NAT + NACLs. Client logs show repeated 502/ECONNRESET.

sara.kim: Which customer/org? Any chance it's the strict egress allowlist one?

alex.cruz: ACME prod (acme-573). Private deployment. Their security team says only outbound 443 to our published egress CIDRs and control-plane allowed. Errors in our logs: `tls: handshake error: EOF` and some connection resets.

gabe: Can they resolve hostnames from their worker nodes? Ask them to run `dig +tcp models.redwood.ai` and `curl -v https://models.redwood.ai/health` from a failing pod.

maria.perez: They ran `dig +tcp models.redwood.ai` and got `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached`. Their infra team admits NACL blocks UDP 53 but they thought TCP 53 was sufficient. Also they mentioned a narrow ephemeral port range on the NAT.

alex.cruz: Packet capture from customer (tcpdump filter: port 443 or port 53) shows SYNs to our edge, then no SYN-ACKs or RST after ~60s. snippet: `17:34:10.123456 IP 10.0.2.23.41000 > 3.248.210.12.443: S` then later `17:35:10.123789 IP 10.0.2.23.41000 > 3.248.210.12.443: R`. Looks like return path or conntrack/NACL state issue. They also show DNS queries failing (UDP 53 timed out).

support-engineer: Steps to validate: 1) Confirm DNS resolution from worker (udp + tcp); 2) Confirm NACL allows ephemeral outbound ports (1024-65535 or at least 32768-61000) for TCP; 3) Confirm SG allows outbound 443; 4) Check for inline TLS inspection. Diagnostic commands to share: `dig +tcp models.redwood.ai`, `curl --resolve models.redwood.ai:443:3.248.210.12 https://models.redwood.ai/ -v`, `openssl s_client -connect 3.248.210.12:443 -servername models.redwood.ai -showcerts`.

sara.kim: They tried `curl --resolve` and saw `SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 3.248.210.12:443` — immediate reset. That points to network reset, possibly NACL or NAT exhaustion. They mentioned a Palo Alto inline FW doing TLS inspect.

gabe: If TLS inspect is enabled it will terminate and re-issue certs. Run `openssl s_client -connect 3.248.210.12:443 -servername models.redwood.ai -showcerts` and check certificate CN/SAN. If the presented cert is the FW's CA or CN != models.redwood.ai then TLS MITM is happening and SNI could be rewritten. Our endpoints expect SNI `models.redwood.ai`.

maria.perez: As a temporary mitigation they increased keepalive and enabled DNS caching on the SDK; that helped for a few minutes (cached IPs), then failures returned under new flows.

alex.cruz: Recommended fix I sent: Allow UDP 53 (or at least ensure TCP DNS fallback works), open ephemeral outbound ports (32768-61000), bypass TLS-inspect for `*.redwood.ai` (or add our certs to allowlist), and ensure NAT gateway has enough ephemeral ports / connection tracking.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT created: #INC-2026-458 (private-egress-tls-dns-nacl) assigned to support-engineer.

support-engineer: Follow-up from customer: they updated NACL to permit UDP 53 and ephemeral 32768-61000, flushed NAT conntrack, and removed TLS-inspect rule for our domains. After NAT flush streams resumed and TLS handshakes succeeded. Closing - will add KB on NACL + TLS-inspect pitfalls.

alex.cruz: Great, please record the exact CIDR/IPs we asked them to permit and the KB steps. Thanks all.
